rows.question: is cataract surgery covered?
rows.reply:
Likely yes — cataract surgery is a listed “specified disease/procedure” and is covered only after the specified‑disease waiting period, with an exception for accidents. 

What that means: your policy’s rules put cataract and other lens/retina disorders on the specified‑disease list and those treatments are excluded until the 24‑month specified‑disease waiting period is complete from your first policy inception. If you want, tell me the cataract surgery/admission date and I will check whether the waiting period is over for that date.

rows.question: is a hospital stay of under 24 hours covered?
rows.reply: Yes — a hospital stay under 24 hours is covered only if it is a recognised Day Care Treatment or a specified procedure; otherwise hospitalization means admission for at least 24 consecutive in‑patient hours. The policy’s day‑care definition covers procedures done in less than 24 hours; the treatment must be medically necessary and prescribed in writing. Tell me the procedure and date and I’ll check whether it qualifies under your policy.
